tour.welcome.title: Welcome to SimFleet ✈️
tour.welcome.body: Let me show you the 5 main screens and the essential settings in under a minute. The tour switches screens for you as you advance. Press "Next" or use the ← → arrows. You can skip anytime.
tour.dashboard.title: 1 · Dashboard
tour.dashboard.body: Your home panel: total installed packages, disk space, top developers and the largest packages. Auto-updates when something changes in your Community folder.
tour.search.title: 2 · Search catalogs
tour.search.body: Search airports, aircraft, liveries and mods on SceneryAddons and Simplaza. Each card shows whether it's already installed and whether an update is available. The selector on the right switches catalogs.
tour.map.title: 3 · World map
tour.map.body: World view with all your installed airports as green dots. Click one to open its details. The amber badge marks the ones with an update available, and you can filter by GSX.
tour.addons.title: 4 · Your addons
tour.addons.body: Aircraft, liveries, instruments and mods you have installed. Filter by type, search by name, and open each one to reinstall or uninstall.
tour.flightbook.title: 5 · FlightBook (real flights)
tour.flightbook.body: Logbook of your MSFS flights, captured automatically through SimConnect. ICAOs, gates, landing FPM, fuel, passengers (via SimBrief OFP) and a flight evaluation. Click a flight to see its real route on the globe. While flying, the orange aircraft marks your current position.
tour.notifications.title: Notifications
tour.notifications.body: Updates available for your packages and the app show up here. The app checks at startup and on focus — no manual buttons.
tour.settings.title: Settings
tour.settings.body: Let's open Settings to see the essentials. Everything lives here: SimBrief, units, folders, backup, cloud, GSX profiles and more.
tour.settings_units.title: Settings · General & units
tour.settings_units.body: Here you pick language, dark/light theme, start with Windows and your SimBrief Pilot ID. Plus per-category units (weight, altitude, speed, distance, pressure, temperature) with quick imperial/metric presets.
tour.settings_folders.title: Settings · Folders
tour.settings_folders.body: The MOST important thing for everything to work: the path to your MSFS 2020 Community folder. Detect it or set it manually here. Without this, the app can't scan your addons.
tour.settings_cloud.title: Settings · Drive sync
tour.settings_cloud.body: Optional: back up and sync your FlightBook with Google Drive across PCs. It has a step-by-step guide and a button to test the connection.
tour.finish.title: Ready for takeoff! 🛫
tour.finish.body: That's it. You can replay this tour anytime from Settings → Tour. Happy flights!

whatsnew.title: What's new in SimFleet
whatsnew.subtitle: flightsim.to integration and more
whatsnew.flightsimto.title: Built-in flightsim.to browser
whatsnew.flightsimto.desc: Search and download add-ons with your own session without leaving SimFleet; they install automatically.
whatsnew.tracking.title: Update alerts
whatsnew.tracking.desc: SimFleet notifies you in the bell when an add-on you downloaded from flightsim.to has a new version.
whatsnew.gsx.title: GSX profiles when installing airports
whatsnew.gsx.desc: When you install an airport it shows the available GSX profiles and flags the most popular and the one compatible with your scenery.
whatsnew.adblock.title: No ads in the built-in browser
whatsnew.adblock.desc: Network-level ad blocking: faster and distraction-free.
whatsnew.liveries.title: Better-classified liveries
whatsnew.liveries.desc: PMDG/iFly liveries are detected as LIVERY, not miscellaneous.
whatsnew.r_preflight.title: Ready to fly? + new scenery radar
whatsnew.r_preflight.body: A Dashboard button cross-checks your next flight (SimBrief OFP or the live sim) against what you have installed: departure and arrival scenery enabled and up to date, current AIRAC… each with a button to fix it. Plus it flags scenery just published in the catalog.
whatsnew.r_palette.title: Global search with Ctrl+K
whatsnew.r_palette.body: Press Ctrl+K (Cmd+K on Mac) from any screen to jump between views, go to an installed aircraft or airport, or search the catalog — all from the keyboard.
whatsnew.r_replay.title: Replay your flights on the map
whatsnew.r_replay.body: Open a flight in the FlightBook and hit “Replay”: an aircraft retraces your real track with a trail, play/pause, speeds and a scrubber to jump anywhere, showing the altitude and speed at each point.
whatsnew.r_cleanup.title: Smart disk cleanup
whatsnew.r_cleanup.body: From the Dashboard, SimFleet cross-checks your scenery against your history and shows the airports you've NEVER flown, sorted by size, so you can uninstall them and reclaim space. You can also manage your landing recordings.
whatsnew.r_share.title: Share your flights + annual Wrapped
whatsnew.r_share.body: Generate a slick card for any flight (copy it or save as PNG) and discover your Wrapped: your year in flights, hours, favorite destinations and aircraft. Plus, export your FlightBook to a self-contained web page to share.
whatsnew.r_fps.title: Your FPS optimizations survive updates
whatsnew.r_fps.body: When an update reinstalls a scenery and wipes your FPS tweaks, SimFleet remembers them and offers to restore them all in one click. And re-scanning Community is now faster.
whatsnew.simbrief.title: Automatic SimBrief (shared account)
whatsnew.simbrief.body: SimFleet now detects your OFP by your email: it links the right plan even if you share the SimBrief account, and refreshes every 30s until the gate. No more linking plans by hand.
whatsnew.simver.title: MSFS 2020 and 2024 together
whatsnew.simver.body: On launch, SimFleet detects which MSFS versions you have installed and filters scenery and Community packages by the right version. You can switch version from Settings.
whatsnew.drop.title: Improved drag & drop
whatsnew.drop.body: Drop .zip/.rar/.7z (even password-protected) or whole folders: SimFleet sorts GSX, Community and others, and installs them in the right folder. When done it can delete the original archive.
whatsnew.flightbook.title: More accurate logbook
whatsnew.flightbook.body: Flight close now waits for real engine shutdown (N2 < 5%) and shows the aircraft's real manufacturer and airline. Your block times and records stay cleaner.
whatsnew.realdata.title: Real sim data
whatsnew.realdata.body: Fleet maintenance is now driven by the REAL telemetry from your flights: engine EGT and oil temperature/pressure (already recorded by the app), brake temperature and touchdown firmness. Each aircraft shows a «Real sim data» strip with its peaks (cycles, hours, EGT, brakes, hardest landing), and tyre/brake/EGT/oil wear comes from that — not a made-up model. Works with PMDG, Fenix, iFly, iniBuilds and the default aircraft; iniBuilds also reports real tyre wear from its own model.
whatsnew.finance2.title: Finance, in more detail
whatsnew.finance2.body: Three Finance upgrades: (1) Balance history — a curve of each airline's «bank» flight by flight, with aircraft purchases and maintenance deducted. (2) Ranking across your airlines — most profitable, best margin and happiest passengers, with medals. (3) Automatic onboard services — each airline manages its services to fit its model (legacy with comfort included, low-cost paid à la carte, cargo with none), reflected in the books, maintenance and PDFs.
whatsnew.settings2.title: Settings reorganized
whatsnew.settings2.body: Settings now have a side menu with each section (General, Flights, Map, Folders, GSX, cloud, backup, storage…). One section shows at a time: you find everything at a glance, no long scroll. Also: F5/Ctrl+R are blocked (no more accidental reloads), changing the MSFS version requires a restart, cargo airline logos (DHL, FedEx…) now show up, and dropping a livery pack with iFly/PMDG configs inside routes those .ini to the correct aircraft folder.
whatsnew.finance.title: Airline Finance (new)
whatsnew.finance.body: Every airline you fly now has a real economy: market value, revenue (tickets/freight + extras) vs costs (fuel, catering, handling, maintenance, taxes and real GSX invoices) and passenger satisfaction — driven by your landings and how you run the fleet. Open it from “Finance” or click an airline in the Hangar. Manage maintenance and onboard services (snacks, wifi, seats, baggage) and watch the numbers move. Cargo and passenger airlines are told apart automatically.
whatsnew.crosslink.title: One scenery for both MSFS 2020 and 2024
whatsnew.crosslink.body: Install a scenery once and SimFleet links it to the other simulator with an NTFS junction: zero copies, 0 MB extra and no admin rights. Deleting the link never touches the original.
whatsnew.hangar.title: Hangar: your fleet, with analytics
whatsnew.hangar.body: Every registration gets its own card: hours, miles, most-flown airports and regions, the FPM trend of your latest landings and landing-gear health. Your pilot career, in data.
whatsnew.recording.title: Best Landings: record and grade every touchdown
whatsnew.recording.body: SimFleet records your landings with native audio (no external ffmpeg) and shows an instant OSD with FPM, G, wind, pitch and roll the moment you touch down. Clips land in a gallery with favorites and scoring.
whatsnew.crewvs.title: Crew VS: fly live against your co-pilot
whatsnew.crewvs.body: If you and another pilot fly the same plan on the same day, you link up in real time: you'll see their aircraft on your map and a duel card with aircraft, airline, registration and who's winning the race.
whatsnew.gsxupd.title: GSX update alerts
whatsnew.gsxupd.body: SimFleet watches your GSX Pro version and lets you know — in the bell and on the dashboard — when FSDT ships a new one. One click opens the FSDT Installer for you. As a safeguard: if the simulator is running, it warns you and will NOT open the installer until you close MSFS, so the install can't get corrupted.
whatsnew.airac.title: AIRAC cycle alerts
whatsnew.airac.body: SimFleet works out the current AIRAC cycle from the official 28-day calendar — no hourly polling — and alerts you when a new one is available. Tapping the notification opens Navigraph Hub so you can update your nav data.
whatsnew.osd.title: The landing OSD, always on top of the sim
whatsnew.osd.body: On touchdown an instant OSD pops up with your FPM, G-force, wind, pitch and roll — now ALWAYS above the simulator and without stealing focus, in both MSFS 2020 and 2024. The FPM color matches the flight detail: butter, acceptable or hard.
whatsnew.crewvs2.title: Crew VS: per-flight history + rival on the map
whatsnew.crewvs2.body: Every flight keeps its own Crew VS: open a finished flight and you'll see the duel for THAT flight (if your co-pilot was also flying that day). When the flight ends and the duel is ready you get a notification in the app and in the bell. And on the map you now see your rival's trail and, by hitting «focus» on their panel, their aircraft is pinned and you follow it live just like your own.
whatsnew.maint.title: Maintenance alerts and a self-sustaining economy
whatsnew.maint.body: When an aircraft has a component near service (75%) or overdue (80%), a card lands in the bell — click it and its workshop opens in Finance. And like real life, a component at 100% cannot keep flying: the airline services it AUTOMATICALLY, the cost hits the books and the history shows in the Hangar. The economic loop closes with no manual input.
whatsnew.settings3.title: Settings: find anything in 5 seconds
whatsnew.settings3.body: The Settings menu was redesigned: 4 clear groups (General, Flight & sim, Data & cloud, Folders & backup) that LIST what they contain, plus a search box that finds any option by name — "msfs version", "units", "backup"… There is also a quick-restart button that reloads the app straight to the splash, without asking for the sim version again.
whatsnew.fpsnotice.title: FPS Optimization on scenery install
whatsnew.fpsnotice.body: When you install a new scenery (download, drag&drop or manual), SimFleet detects whether it ships optional toggleable objects (static aircraft, passengers, GSE, clutter…) and notifies you in the bell. One click opens the performance modal — the same as the Link Map wrench — to turn off what you do not need and gain FPS.

settings.cloud.guide.s1.title: Create a Google Cloud project
settings.cloud.guide.s2.title: Enable the Google Drive API on THAT project
settings.cloud.guide.s2.body: VERIFY the project selector at the top shows YOUR project (from step 1). Click Enable and wait 30 s. Open:
settings.cloud.guide.s3.title: Configure the OAuth Consent Screen
settings.cloud.guide.s3.body: User Type: External. Set the app name and your email as support. Under Test Users ADD YOUR OWN EMAIL (without it, Google blocks consent in Testing mode). Open:
settings.cloud.guide.s4.title: Create the Desktop OAuth Client
settings.cloud.guide.s4.body: Create Credentials → OAuth Client ID → Application type: Desktop app (NOT Web). Copy the Client ID and Client Secret. Open:
settings.cloud.guide.s5.title: Paste the credentials in this app
settings.cloud.guide.s5.body: Above in this same panel → "Configure / Change" → paste both values → Save.
settings.cloud.guide.s6.title: Connect
settings.cloud.guide.s6.body: Click "Connect with Google" → your browser opens → pick your account → on "Google hasn’t verified this app" click Advanced → Go to app (unsafe) — normal in Testing mode. Approve ALL scopes (drive.appdata + userinfo.email).
settings.cloud.guide.s7.title: Test connection
settings.cloud.guide.s7.body: If you connected but "Sync now" fails, click "Test connection" — it tells you step by step where it breaks (credentials, refresh token, identity, Drive API, scope, listing).
settings.cloud.guide.err403.title: Still getting 403 after enabling the Drive API:
settings.cloud.guide.err403.b1: Check the Drive API is enabled on THE SAME project from step 1.
settings.cloud.guide.err403.b2: Click Disconnect + Connect again — the cached access token may lack the new scopes.
settings.cloud.guide.err403.b3: Revoke your app’s access, then reconnect:
